discovered_out_of_scope_issues: packages/core/package.json main/types still point to src/index.ts (source .ts) rather than the compiled dist entrypoint; not required by this task but downstream Node consumers would need the runtime path. notes_for_reviewer: Encoder uses an explicit hand-rolled UTF-8 encoder rather than the runtime TextEncoder so it is portable across V8 configurations and avoids adding @types/node or the DOM lib to the pure core tsconfig.

Cycle detection uses a per-encode Set that is add-before/delete-after; sibling occurrences of the same reference are admitted (test 'sibling occurrences of the same reference are not treated as cyclic').

Tests import the compiled dist from packages/core/dist/index.js and rely on Node's CJS-from-ESM named-export interop; a pretest npm script now runs compile before tests so a clean checkout can npm test without a separate compile step. CI already runs compile before test, so the pretest is a no-op there.

encodingVersion is a caller-provided string; the ADR treats it as opaque and does not prescribe a bump policy — that continues to belong in the Definition of Done and future ADRs when the format evolves.
ADR §10 (Non-goals) documents that StateHash and finalTick exclusion belong outside this ADR, matching INV-22's requirement that finalTick be excluded 'outside this encoder'.
payload.summary: Wrote ADR-009 with a byte-level canonical encoding grammar (envelope magic "CE1", LEB128 length framing, ten type tags, UTF-8 key ordering, safe-integer vs bigint distinction, explicit-sign bigint decimal, rejection rules, cycle handling, encodingVersion participation). Implemented CanonicalEncoder in packages/core with an explicit UTF-8 encoder (no TextEncoder dependency), a growing byte buffer, deterministic CanonicalEncoderError with typed codes, and a stateless top-level canonicalEncode(value, {encodingVersion}). Exported the encoder, error class, tag table, magic bytes, and value/option types from packages/core/src/index.ts. Added a 50-case test suite covering envelope, tag table, golden vectors for every admitted primitive and container, permutation-invariance, UTF-8 vs UTF-16/locale key ordering, integer/bigint collision-freeness, ordered-vs-unordered semantics, encodingVersion sensitivity, and rejection of every prohibited value plus cyclic containers. Wired the suite into npm test and added a pretest hook that compiles before running tests so the compiled entrypoint is always fresh.
